display: Hotel concierge in Dubai, from Batangas in the Philippines. I love my work and my regular guests, and I'm learning Arabic.

signals.text: I work twelve-hour shifts six days a week and I'm tired. The little kindnesses from guests are what carry me.
I'm learning Arabic at lunch with a colleague, and I want more chances to practise real conversation.
I want to open a small bakery in Batangas one day, and I'm still far from the savings it needs.
I've been looking at second-hand bakery equipment, but I don't know what a realistic first step looks like.
Singing in my church choir is the one time I stop thinking about money. I'd like to sing more, and better.
I send about half my salary home every month and I'd like to find cheaper, smarter ways to do it.
I share a room in Al Barsha and can't afford my own place. I'd like to find a quieter, cheaper living arrangement.
I sometimes feel stuck in a loop of working and sending money home, and I wonder when I'll be able to stop.
My mother keeps asking when I will come home, and I don't have an answer yet.
My residence permit renewal is coming up in mid-October, and I'd like to get through it smoothly.
I only get Fridays off, and I keep them for church. I have almost no free time to meet new people.

offers.text: Six years of five-star hotel concierge experience in Dubai. I can advise on guest service, handling difficult requests and remembering what people prefer.
I speak English and Tagalog, conversational Arabic and a little Russian. I can help Filipino newcomers or visitors get around Dubai in everyday terms.
I can suggest where to eat, what to book and how to plan a stay in Dubai, especially around Jumeirah.
I've built a method for tracking regulars' preferences in a notebook of 300+ names. I can teach the approach for hospitality or small-business customer care, without sharing any guest's details.
I sing in a church choir and can join or lead Filipino hymns and community singing.
I know the practical side of working in Dubai as a Filipino in hospitality: life in Al Barsha, remittance routines, and how to handle the first months.
I have a UAE bank account and a Philippines remittance route, so I can share what has worked in sending money home.
I can offer calm, patient company to someone who is tired or homesick. I've been through that myself.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a pastry chef or baker with a few years of experience. I'd happily share a beginner's plan for a small neighbourhood bakery: equipment, costs, and what to buy first and what to skip.
catchers.can: Marites could use that plan to work out realistic steps toward her Batangas bakery. She can also give feedback on what a customer-facing counter and service should feel like.
catchers.confirm: Is your advice aimed at a very small, low-capital bakery, such as a one-oven shop in a Philippine town?

catchers.hypo: Hello, I'm an Arab-speaking person who wants to practise English or Tagalog with a friendly learner. I could do a short weekly conversation exchange.
catchers.can: Marites can offer English and Tagalog practice in return for Arabic conversation. Her colleague Khalid already teaches her the basics, so she can start from greetings and menu words.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for an informal conversation exchange for 20 to 30 minutes, rather than formal paid tutoring?

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a Filipino engineer or lecturer. I'm looking for engineering students in the Philippines to mentor or recommend for internships.
catchers.can: Marites can pass this to her younger brother Jun, who is studying engineering in the Philippines, so he can reach out himself.
catchers.confirm: Is your offer open to undergraduate engineering students based in the Philippines?

catchers.hypo: I'm visiting Dubai with my family for a week and want a local who can tell me how to avoid the tourist traps and where to get good food near Jumeirah.
catchers.can: Marites can give a practical, honest plan for the stay, including where to eat, how to get around, and what not to waste money on.
catchers.confirm: Is your stay in Dubai, and do you mostly need advice about the Jumeirah or Al Barsha area?

catchers.hypo: We run a small hotel or hospitality team and want to build a simple system for remembering guest preferences. Could you tell us how you do it?
catchers.can: Marites can explain her notebook method and how she decides which details are worth noting, and what should be left alone.
catchers.confirm: Do you want a practical method for a small team, rather than a software product?

catchers.hypo: I'm a Filipino working abroad and I just moved to Dubai. I don't know anyone, my days off are strange, and I'd like to find a church community or a choir.
catchers.can: Marites can welcome a newcomer to her church service and choir, and explain the basics of living and working in Dubai.
catchers.confirm: Are you a Filipino newcomer in Dubai who is looking for a church or choir community?

catchers.hypo: I run a low-fee remittance or savings service for overseas Filipino workers and I'm looking for honest feedback from users who send money home every month.
catchers.can: Marites can give practical feedback as a monthly sender who compares options, and she can introduce colleagues and friends in the same situation.
catchers.confirm: Is your service aimed at overseas workers who send money to the Philippines regularly?

forbids.text: I can't take extra jobs or side work, because my hotel contract forbids it.
I have only one day off a week, Friday, and I keep it for church, so I can't take Friday meetings.
My visa is tied to the hotel, so I can't move jobs or leave Dubai freely.
I won't share any guest's name, preferences or private details, however useful it would be.
I won't invest in or lend money for anything that promises quick returns.

projects.name: Batangas bakery
projects.text: A small neighbourhood bakery in Batangas, in the long run. It is still at the planning stage, and I am saving toward it.

policy.t1: When a collaboration looks promising, I will share my schedule, languages, church choir, hospitality know-how and small side interests.
policy.t2: When I'm fairly sure and know who the other person is, I will share my bakery goal and savings target, and that I support my family back home.
policy.never: My bank balance, my family's medical bills and any guest's private details.
